author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose missing shadows without stacking graphics hacks
summary: Capture one shadow-heavy scene at native resolution, identify whether the absent layer is geometry, depth, or blending, compare hardware APIs and a software reference, then retain only the smallest per-game correction.
heroAlt: PCSX2 comparison capture from a graphics accuracy fix in a shadowed game scene

sourceLabels.pcsx2-performance: PCSX2 graphics counters and setting indicators

blocks.text: Prove which shadow layer is absent

A shadow can be a projected texture, a translucent framebuffer pass, ordinary dark geometry, or an effect combined with depth testing. The useful first question is therefore not which hack to enable, but whether the game draws the layer at all. Choose a place where the same character, light, and camera can be restored reliably. Record the game serial, active renderer, GPU driver, internal resolution, blending setting, and any inherited per-game fixes before touching the profile.
Do not judge the change from a different time of day, camera angle, save state, or animation frame. Dynamic lighting can make two valid frames look like a renderer regression.

items: A normal in-game save immediately before a repeatable lit scene.
One baseline screenshot with the character and ground visible together.
Native internal resolution and post-processing disabled for the first comparison.
The system GPU driver selected; custom drivers are a separate experiment.
A written copy of global and per-game graphics overrides.

blocks.text: Separate draw, blend, and depth behavior

items: 1. Cold-boot the title and capture the baseline checkpoint without loading an emulator save state.
2. Reset manual GS fixes for this title, select native internal resolution, and replay the same movement path.
3. Switch only between the supported hardware APIs, closing the game between runs so the renderer initializes cleanly.
4. If both hardware paths omit the layer, use software rendering briefly as a correctness reference and capture the identical camera.
5. When software shows the shadow, return to the more stable hardware API and raise blending accuracy by one tier only.
6. If blending changes nothing, restore it and test the documented depth-related correction appropriate to the title instead of combining guesses.
7. Repeat a second shadow scene that uses a different surface or light source.
8. Warm the device for ten minutes and confirm the selected correction remains fast enough for actual play.

blocks.text: Software output is diagnostic evidence, not a promise of playable speed. A correct software frame shows that the disc image and game code can produce the effect, while a hardware-only failure narrows the search to renderer behavior. A blending change that restores a translucent shadow is different from a depth fix that restores geometry hidden by ordering. Keeping those branches separate makes the result explainable and reversible.
Accept the profile only when the layer is stable in more than the original test frame.

items: Shadow position follows the moving subject rather than remaining as a stale rectangle.
Opacity resembles the software reference and does not darken the entire ground pass.
Nearby decals, fog, and HUD transparency remain intact.
The effect survives a cold boot and a later area transition.
Sustained speed and frame pacing remain within the recorded baseline budget.
The shadow is absent in software too: verify the image and confirm the original scene really contains one.
Only emulator save-state loading breaks it: retest from an in-game save and discard the incompatible state.
Every dark surface disappears: reset broad skip-draw or manual GS overrides.
The fix works once but fails after resume: capture renderer and driver details for a lifecycle report.

blocks.text: Return to the measured graphics baseline

Restore automatic blending, disable the tested depth correction, reselect the original renderer and system driver, and cold-boot the checkpoint. Keep the before-and-after captures with their settings, but delete temporary save states that cannot reproduce the scene consistently.
Do not publish copyrighted save or disc data

A support report can include the serial, settings, logs, and user-created screenshots where permitted. Do not attach a game image, firmware, encryption material, or a save containing third-party distributed content merely to demonstrate the shadow.
